_comment: The outside tools `cv` runs over the deployment files it read (backlog 0693; ADR-157, Later and As built, 21 November 2026). Read by the runner of `sv`'s own outside tools (`sv_check::adapters`, ADR-018), in the same shape as data/adapters.json, and kept apart from it so that `sv`'s list is unchanged. Each tool is handed the files `cv` read, by name, or the folder; is run so that it opens no network connection (measured in the sandbox, which reports each connection a program tries); and is given a settings file of `cv`'s own, so the app's cannot turn its rules off unseen. Rules are mapped one at a time after reading the requirement. Most container-hardening rules speak to no ASVS 5.0 requirement, as `cv.container-root` does not (the owner's choice, 20 November 2026): they are mapped for what they detect and cite nothing. A secret in a Dockerfile's ARG or ENV is evidence against V13.3.1 and never credits it, since finding none does not show that a vault is used. A rule not here is a finding carrying no requirement.

adapters.name: hadolint
adapters.note: Measured with hadolint 2.15.1 on 21 November 2026. Without a settings file of its own it reads the app's `.hadolint.yaml` from where it runs, whose `ignored` list hid DL3007, and a `# hadolint ignore=` comment hid DL3008: it is given `cv`'s settings file (`-c`, which it reads in place of the app's) and `--disable-ignore-pragma`, and both rules came back. It opened no connection. It exits 1 when it finds something and 0 when it does not. A file it cannot parse is reported as DL1000, with exit 1, so that is a finding rather than a quiet run. It is handed `cv`'s Dockerfiles by name.

DL1000.what: hadolint could not read this Dockerfile, so its other rules did not run over it

DL3002.what: the last USER of the Dockerfile is root

DL3007.what: the base image is named by its `latest` tag, so what is built can change without the file changing

DL3064.what: a value that looks like a secret is set in the Dockerfile's ARG or ENV, where it is kept in the image

adapters.name: Checkov
adapters.note: Measured with Checkov 3.4.6 on 21 November 2026. Run as it comes, it asked api0.prismacloud.io for its rules' guidance four times; `--skip-download` stops that, with the same results. It reads the app's `.checkov.yaml`, which hid CKV_DOCKER_2 whatever `--config-file` said, from the folder it scans and from where it runs, and it must run in the app's folder to be handed files by name: so while that file is there, a run that finds nothing is not credited (`switched_off_by`). A `# checkov:skip=` comment leaves the result in its report, marked as suppressed. It writes its report as `results_sarif.sarif` in the folder `--output-file-path` names (`report_in_database`). It exits 1 when a check failed and 0 when none did. Given a Terraform plan it cannot parse it says nothing and exits 0, which is why it is handed only the files `cv` read.

CKV_DOCKER_7.what: the base image is named by its `latest` tag, or by no tag

CKV_DOCKER_8.what: the last USER of the Dockerfile is root

CKV_K8S_14.what: a Kubernetes container's image is named by its `latest` tag, or by no tag

CKV_K8S_19.what: a Kubernetes pod shares the host's network namespace

CKV_K8S_20.what: a Kubernetes container allows privilege escalation

CKV_K8S_23.what: a Kubernetes container is allowed to run as root

adapters.name: Trivy
adapters.note: Measured with Trivy 0.74.0 on 21 November 2026. Its configuration rules are the ones built into the program (`--skip-check-update`; the owner's choice, 21 November 2026), so a report names the version whose rules ran. With that alone it still connected to check.trivy.dev; `--skip-version-check` and `--disable-telemetry` stop that, with the same results. It reads `trivy.yaml` and `.trivyignore` from where it runs: the app's `trivy.yaml` turned the run into no results at all, and its `.trivyignore` hid DS-0026. It is given `cv`'s settings file for both, and every rule came back. It is given the folder, since `trivy config` takes one target; it did not follow a link in it to a file outside. It exits 0 whether or not it finds something, and 1 when it fails.

DS-0001.what: the base image is named by its `latest` tag

DS-0031.what: a secret is passed in through build arguments or environment variables, or a secret file is copied into the image

KSV-0001.what: a Kubernetes container can raise its own privileges

KSV-0009.what: a Kubernetes pod uses the host's network

KSV-0012.what: a Kubernetes container runs as root

KSV-0013.what: a Kubernetes container's image is named by its `latest` tag
